title: US midterms: Democrats flip North Carolina Senate seat as early results favour them in House
dek: Roy Cooper's win is the first Senate seat to change hands, and Democrats hold Georgia and New Hampshire. Control of both chambers was still undecided at 8.20 am IST, with exit polls putting Trump's approval at 38%.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Democrats took the first Senate seat to change hands in the US midterm elections, as former governor Roy Cooper won North Carolina's open seat, the Associated Press projected. Early results on Wednesday morning, India time, pointed to gains for the party in the House of Representatives. Neither chamber had been called by about 8.20 am IST, and several Senate races that will decide the majority were still being counted.

The early picture is bad for President Donald Trump's party. Democrats held Senate seats in Georgia, New Hampshire and Virginia, flipped Georgia's governorship and picked up several Republican-held House seats. Exit polls cited by CBS News put Trump's approval at 38%, which CBS said was on course to be a record low for a president at a midterm election. The result will shape the last two years of Trump's term, including his options on the war with Iran, which matters directly to India's oil supplies and its seafarers in the Gulf.

## What happened

The AP called the Georgia Senate race for the Democratic incumbent Jon Ossoff over Republican Mike Collins at about 7.39 pm Eastern time (6.09 am IST); Collins conceded. In New Hampshire, Democrat Chris Pappas beat Republican John Sununu for the seat left open by Jeanne Shaheen's retirement, and Sununu conceded, NBC News reported. Mark Warner held Virginia and Cory Booker held New Jersey for the Democrats.

In North Carolina, Cooper defeated Republican Michael Whatley for the seat being vacated by Republican Thom Tillis, a call the AP made at 8.23 pm Eastern (6.53 am IST); Whatley conceded. Republicans held Florida, where Ashley Moody won the special election for the seat once held by Marco Rubio, and safe seats including Kentucky, Oklahoma, West Virginia, Wyoming and Tennessee, according to NBC News.

The Senate races still open at the time of writing included Texas, where Democrat James Talarico faces Republican Ken Paxton; Ohio; South Carolina, where Democrat Annie Andrews is challenging Republican Darline Graham; and Kansas. NBC's Decision Desk rated all four as leaning towards the Democrats on early returns, and CNBC's election desk said the same of Texas, Ohio and South Carolina. These are projections from partial counts, not calls. Maine, where Republican Susan Collins is defending her seat, was rated a toss-up by CBS, which said ranked-choice counting could take longer. Michigan, Iowa and Alaska were also undecided.

In the House, CNBC's election desk said control "leans Democratic". It projected that Democrats would win at least 210 seats; 218 are needed for a majority. NBC reported Democratic gains in Pennsylvania's 8th, Colorado's 8th, New Jersey's 7th and North Carolina's 11th districts, and a win in a toss-up seat in Florida's redrawn 22nd district. Democrats also held two Florida seats that a Republican-drawn map had targeted.

In the governors' races, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia, which last elected a Democratic governor in 1998, and Republican Byron Donalds won Florida, the AP projected.

## Background

Republicans went into the election holding the Senate 53-47, counting two independents who vote with the Democrats. A Senate majority needs 51 seats, because Vice-President JD Vance breaks 50-50 ties for the Republicans. With North Carolina flipped, Democrats need to flip three more Republican seats and hold Michigan to take control, CBS News said. In the House, Republicans held 218 seats to the Democrats' 214, so a net Democratic gain of three seats would change control.

The election was fought over prices and over the war with Iran, now in its ninth month. In a CNBC voter poll, 74% of respondents called Iran a crucial or major factor in their vote, and 62% said the military action had been the wrong decision. In the same poll, 65% said tariffs had hurt the national economy and 22% said they had helped. CNBC, citing AAA, put the national average petrol price at about $4.15 a gallon, against $2.98 before the war.

## Reactions

Cooper said voters had seen that "the chaos and corruption in Washington were hurting our people". Tillis, the outgoing Republican senator, congratulated him and said he looked forward to working with him, CNBC reported. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said his party was "on the verge" of winning the House but would "take nothing for granted", CBS reported.

On the Republican side, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis called the Iran war a "big, big drag" on his party, CNBC reported. Before the polls closed, Trump said in a phone interview that he held "the ultimate power", meaning the presidential veto, CBS reported; a White House official described the mood as "defiant". House Speaker Mike Johnson had said before the vote that the polls were wrong. Trump has no public events scheduled for Wednesday.

## Why it matters for India

Iran is the most direct link. Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday that he had no immediate plan to resume strikes on Iran, while The New York Times reported that the military was ready to begin as early as Wednesday (see our separate report). A Congress controlled by Democrats could try to limit the war through funding and war-powers votes, although Trump could veto such measures. Any return to fighting would hit shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, on which India's imports of oil and gas rely heavily, and Indian crews in the Gulf. An Indian seafarer was killed in an attack on an Indian-flagged vessel off Oman this week.

Trade is the second link. A Democratic House would gain the power to investigate and hold hearings on Trump's tariff policy, which shapes India's trade talks with Washington, though tariff decisions would stay largely with the White House.

Markets were cautious. US stock futures fell about 0.5% after the first polls closed, CNBC reported. GIFT Nifty pointed to a slightly lower opening for Indian shares on Wednesday after four straight days of gains, Zee Business reported.

## What happens next

Counting continues through the day in India. The last polls, in Alaska's western Aleutian Islands, close at 1 am Eastern time (11.30 am IST). Close races, especially Maine with its ranked-choice count and Alaska, may take days to settle. The National Republican Senatorial Committee has started raising money for a possible recount in Alaska, CNBC reported. The new Congress takes office on 3 January 2027.

## Key numbers

- 51: Senate seats needed for a majority. Republicans held 53 before the vote
- 218: House seats needed for a majority. Democrats were projected at 210 or more (CNBC)
- 1: Senate seat flipped so far (North Carolina, to the Democrats)
- 38%: Trump's approval in early exit polls (CBS News)
- $11.87 billion: political ad spending this cycle, a record (AdImpact, via CNBC)
